OSTEOLOGY 1The Skull

Lecturer: Shaoyu Wang (Shaun), PhD, BVetMed — Senior Lecturer in Anatomy & Physiology.

1 · Overview of the skull

  • The skull = cranium + mandible.
  • Most complicated bony structure in the human body.
  • 22 individual bones — 8 paired and 6 single — plus 3 paired ear ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes).
  • Functions: protect the brain; support visceral functions (sight, smell, hearing, mastication).

Cranium is described as:

  • Cranial vault (calvaria)
  • Cranial base
  • Cranial cavity
  • Facial skeleton

Developmental division:

  • Neurocranium — houses the brain, 8 bones: frontal, parietal (×2), temporal (×2), occipital, sphenoid, ethmoid.
  • Viscerocranium — facial skeleton, 15 bones: mandible, ethmoid, vomer, maxillae (×2), inferior nasal conchae (×2), zygomatic (×2), palatine (×2), nasal (×2), lacrimal (×2).

6 single (unpaired) bones

  • Occipital
  • Frontal
  • Sphenoid
  • Ethmoid
  • Vomer
  • Mandible

8 paired bones

  • Parietal
  • Temporal
  • Zygomatic
  • Maxilla
  • Lacrimal
  • Nasal
  • Inferior nasal concha
  • Palatine

7 · Base of the skull — Norma basalis

Divided into anterior, middle and posterior parts.

Anterior part

  • Teeth & alveolar processes
  • Hard palate = palatine processes of maxilla + horizontal plates of palatine
  • Sutures: intermaxillary, palatomaxillary, interpalatine
  • Incisive fossa / canal (nasopalatine)
  • Greater palatine foramen
  • Lesser palatine foramen
  • Posterior nasal spine, pyramidal process

Middle & posterior parts

Middle part:

  • Anterior ½ — vomer & sphenoid bone
  • Posterior ½ — occipital & temporal bone

Posterior part: occipital bone around the foramen magnum, occipital condyles, nuchal lines.

8 · Cranial cavity — the three fossae

Anterior cranial fossa

  • Cribriform plate of ethmoid
  • Crista galli
  • Orbital plates of frontal bone
  • Anterior clinoid process

Middle cranial fossa

  • Optic canal, pituitary (hypophyseal) fossa
  • Foramen rotundum, foramen ovale, foramen spinosum
  • Foramen lacerum, carotid canal
  • Grooves for middle meningeal artery
  • Anterior & posterior clinoid processes

Posterior cranial fossa

  • Foramen magnum
  • Internal auditory (acoustic) meatus
  • Jugular foramen
  • Hypoglossal canal
  • Grooves for transverse, sigmoid & inferior petrosal venous sinuses

10 · Temporal & infratemporal fossae

Temporal fossaInfratemporal fossa Pterygomaxillary fissureSphenopalatine foramen

11 · Foramina of the cranial cavity

  • Cribriform plate — CN I (olfactory)
  • Optic canal — CN II (optic)
  • Foramen rotundum — V2 (maxillary)
  • Foramen ovale — V3 (mandibular)
  • Foramen spinosum — middle meningeal artery
  • Foramen lacerum — covered by cartilage
  • Internal acoustic meatus — CN VII & VIII
  • Jugular foramen — internal jugular vein, CN IX, X, XI
  • Hypoglossal canal — CN XII
  • Foramen magnum — brainstem / spinal cord

12 · Foramina of the cranial base (external)

  • Incisive foramen — nasopalatine branch of V2
  • Greater palatine foramen — greater palatine branch of V2
  • Lesser palatine foramen — lesser palatine branch of V2
  • Foramen ovale, foramen spinosum, foramen lacerum
  • Carotid canal — internal carotid artery
  • Jugular foramen
  • Stylomastoid foramen — facial nerve

13 · Skull at birth (fontanelles)

  • Anterior fontanelle — largest; closes ~18–24 months
  • Posterior fontanelle — closes ~1–3 months
  • Sphenoidal (anterolateral) fontanelle
  • Mastoid (posterolateral) fontanelle
  • Frontal (metopic) suture — between the two frontal halves

Nasal bone

Frontonasal sutureNasionPiriform aperture

Vomer

Single bone forming the posteroinferior part of the nasal septum; articulates above with the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid.

Lacrimal bone

Small, rectangular, very thin & fragile bone in the medial wall of the orbit; helps form the lacrimal fossa / nasolacrimal canal.
